critical_code_review_comments: ScrollToTop and Navbar useEffect callbacks now correctly use block-body arrows so they always return undefined; this is the proper fix for the extension-induced React 19 destroy-not-a-function crash. Consider adding an ESLint rule (react-hooks/exhaustive-deps + custom rule to disallow implicit-return arrows in useEffect) to prevent regressions.

AuthContext calls /api/auth/me on load producing expected 401s in console when unauthenticated -- harmless but noisy; could be silenced by treating 401 as an expected 'no session' state without logging.

rca of the issue: Original crash was in App.js ScrollToTop: `useEffect(() => window.scrollTo(0,0), [pathname])` implicit-return arrow returned whatever window.scrollTo returned. A browser extension in the user's Chrome monkey-patched window.scrollTo to return an object. React 19 treated that object as an effect cleanup fn and called .destroy() on it on next unmount -> TypeError. Fix: convert to block-body `useEffect(() => { window.scrollTo(0,0); }, [pathname])` (returns undefined). Same fix applied to Navbar's setOpen effect. Verified: no crash across single + repeated SPA navigations.
